findings.title: User email_verified_at Cannot Be Set Via Mass Assignment
findings.evidence: User::create() attempts to set 'email_verified_at' => now(), but User model guards this field (User.php line 47), causing it to be silently ignored during mass assignment.
findings.consequence: New user accounts are created with NULL email_verified_at, preventing owner login even after password reset. Owner is locked out and cannot manage their business.
findings.correction: After User::create(), explicitly set $user->email_verified_at = now(); $user->save(); to bypass mass-assignment protection for this admin-controlled operation.
findings.triggeringPath: Admin creates business with new owner email → User created with NULL email_verified_at → Owner resets password → Owner attempts login → Laravel auth blocks unverified email → Owner locked out

findings.title: User role and is_active Cannot Be Set Via Mass Assignment
findings.evidence: User::create() attempts to set 'role' => 'user' and 'is_active' => true, but both fields are in the $guarded array (User.php lines 39, 42), causing them to be silently ignored.
findings.consequence: User account defaults to NULL role and false is_active. Authentication middleware or business logic may reject login attempts from users with invalid role or inactive status.
findings.correction: After User::create(), explicitly set $user->role = 'user'; $user->is_active = true; $user->save(); to properly configure the account for business owner access.
findings.triggeringPath: Admin creates business with new owner email → User created with NULL role and is_active=false → Owner resets password → Owner attempts login → Middleware blocks inactive/invalid role user → Owner locked out
